paper_sections.title: Brain Reactivity to Smoking Cues Prior to Smoking Cessation Predicts Ability to Maintain Tobacco Abstinence
Region-of-Interest (ROI) Analyses: Relation to Smoking Cessation Outcome and Emotional Stroop Performance
Correlations Between FMRI and Emotional Stroop Data

description.value: The study examined whether prequit fMRI reactivity to smoking-related images, emotional Stroop attentional bias, and insula-containing network connectivity could identify nicotine-dependent women who would slip during a subsequent smoking cessation attempt.

design.value: Before quitting smoking, 21 nicotine-dependent women underwent fMRI while viewing smoking-related and neutral images and completed a computerized emotional Stroop task. After a quit attempt, participants were grouped according to whether they smoked after attaining at least 24 hours of abstinence.

description.value: Subjects reported word color while ignoring word meaning; reaction times and accuracies were recorded. Smoking-related interference was computed as Accuracy Neutral − Accuracy Smoking and RT Smoking − RT Neutral.
Expired CO levels were measured at screening and weekly during smoking cessation.

source_definition.value: Fagerstrom Test for Nicotine Dependence scores

description.value: Twenty-one women underwent neuroimaging before participating in a smoking cessation clinical trial.

inclusion_criteria.value: met DSM-IV criteria for current nicotine dependence
reported smoking ≥10 cigarettes per day in the previous 6 months
expired air carbon monoxide (CO) >10 ppmv at screening

exclusion_criteria.value: current unstable medical illness, pregnancy, recent drug and alcohol use, major depressive disorder, alcohol use disorder in the prior 6 months, current psychotropic drug use, or lifetime diagnosis of organic mental or psychotic disorders

recruitment_method.value: participating in a smoking cessation clinical trial at Massachusetts General Hospital

clinical_characteristics.value: reported smoking ≥10 cigarettes per day in the previous 6 months

medication_status.value: nicotine patch (21 mg/day for 4 weeks, 14 mg/day for 2 weeks, 7 mg/day for 2 weeks), and 2-mg nicotine polacrilex gum or lozenge, up to 12 mg/day, to be used as needed

description.value: participants who smoked any cigarettes during the nicotine replacement therapy treatment period following 24 hours abstinence

inclusion_criteria.value: smoked any cigarettes during the nicotine replacement therapy treatment period after at least 24 hours abstinence

description.value: participants who did not smoke during the nicotine replacement therapy treatment period after attaining at least 24 hours of abstinence

inclusion_criteria.value: did not smoke during the nicotine replacement therapy treatment period after at least 24 hours abstinence

task_description.value: During fMRI, subjects viewed smoking-related or neutral images. Animal images were shown to prompt subjects to press a response button and were included to ensure subjects attended to stimuli but were not used in data analyses.

stimuli.value: 42 smoking-related, 40 neutral, and 8 animal images; smoking-related images depicted people smoking, hands holding cigarettes, or cigarettes alone.

task_performance_measures.value: response button presses to animal images

task_description.value: Smoking-related and neutral words, matched for length and use frequency in the English language, were displayed in red, green, or blue fonts. Four 33-trial experimental blocks were run in the following word order: neutral, smoking, smoking, neutral.

instructions.value: report word color as quickly and accurately as possible and ignore word meaning

instrument.value: Siemens Trio 3 Tesla scanner (Erlangen, Germany) with a circularly polarized head coil

description.value: Multiplanar rapidly acquired gradient-echo structural images; TR = 2.1 sec, TE = 2.7 msec, slices = 128, matrix = 256 × 256, flip angle = 12°, resolution = 1.0 × 1.0 × 1.33 mm.

instrument.value: Siemens Trio 3 Tesla scanner (Erlangen, Germany) with a circularly polarized head coil

description.value: Gradient echo echo-planar images; TR = 2 sec, TE = 30 msec, matrix = 64 × 64 mm, field of view = 224, flip angle = 75°, slices = 30, resolution = 3.5 mm isotropic with 0 mm gap.
Images were slice-time corrected, motion corrected, spatially smoothed, resampled, and spatially normalized into Talairach space. Time points exhibiting motion >1.75 mm were modeled out.

steps.value: spatially smoothed with a 6-mm Gaussian kernel
time points exhibiting motion >1.75 mm were modeled out

model_settings.value: Image regressors for smoking, neutral, and animal images and motion confound regressors; beta maps comparing smoking with neutral images were created for each subject and compared between groups using a random-effects analysis.

estimator.value: fixed-effects GLM followed by random-effects analysis

model_type.value: Pearson's correlation coefficient and discriminant analysis

model_settings.value: Beta weights for smoking image > neutral image contrasts were extracted from anterior insula, dACC, DLPFC, and amygdala ROIs and averaged across all voxels within each ROI. Discriminant analysis used leave-one-out cross-validation.

estimator.value: Pearson's correlation coefficient; leave-one-out classification strategy

model_settings.value: Principal-component analysis data reduction; data concatenation; group spatial ICA using the infomax algorithm; 25 optimal components determined by the minimum description length algorithm. Component Number 2 containing bilateral insula and anterior cingulate was selected.

Group (slip, abstinent) as between-subject factor, Condition (neutral vs. smoking-related words) as repeated measures, and FTND scores as covariates; analyses were run separately on accuracy and reaction time.

interpretations.value: Prequit brain reactivity to smoking-related images is greater in smokers who eventually slip after attaining brief abstinence with NRT.
